chapters.fx: What to watch: the Sunday 5pm CT reopen — the first price test of Saturday's maritime escalation; watch USD/JPY and USD/CHF for haven gaps. Monday is Columbus Day: US bond markets are closed, Japan and Canada shut — thin liquidity amplifies moves while FX spot trades normally. Then the real week: RBA minutes Monday 7:30pm CT, US CPI Wednesday 7:30am CT (consensus 3.6% y/y, core 2.5% — the key number is core m/m at 0.2%), Fed Chair Warsh speaks Thursday 10:30pm CT — his read on the prints decides whether the hawkish hold becomes a hike. On the diplomacy side: Iran's formal reply to the US counterproposal is due 'within days,' and whether Trump picks up Putin's broker channel.
chapters.meaning: What changed: the maritime campaign widened on two fronts Saturday. The IRGC navy claimed a supertanker hit naval mines while exiting Hormuz via an 'unauthorized' route — the first mine use of the campaign, but the vessel is unnamed and no independent source has confirmed the blast: treat it as a claim, not a fact. Separately verified: a US fighter jet disabled the Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman with a precision stern strike after it ignored blockade warnings (Reuters), and UKMTO confirmed a Marshall Islands-flagged tanker struck by projectile Saturday evening — the 18th confirmed Iranian hit since Sept 29. CENTCOM says 4 vessels disabled, 135 turned around, and 10 IRGC-linked shadow tankers destroyed since July 14. Thread: the hawkish hold is in week four — Dec ~80% priced, Oct ~18% (CME FedWatch, Oct 7), claims held 197k for a fourth straight week; Saturday added the Riyadh airport strikes (toll now 12 killed and 309 wounded — GACA's Sunday count), Trump's flip on joining the Saudi campaign, and Putin's broker offer. What it means: confirms the thesis. Saturday added no Fed-relevant data — the dollar's path into CPI week is unchanged — but the haven bid arrives at Sunday's reopen with a thicker geopolitical premium and a genuine two-way ledger: escalation (mines, tanker #18, Ocean Molica) against the diplomacy side (Putin's broker channel, Trump's no-strike-before-midterms pledge).

What it means: confirms and sharpens — the haven catalyst is re-armed, but the crowd is already long yen and the yield gap caps rallies. The dollar side of the pair (see the USD chapter) decides the gap; the Gulf decides the fear.

chapters.fx: What to watch: the spread itself — past $15 means Hormuz risk is back in force; toward $5 means the premium is truly unwinding. Sunday's reopen is the first price test of the mine claim and UKMTO 162-26. On the diplomacy side: if Putin's broker channel gains traction, the premium softens — that's the path to a sub-$100 Brent and a collapsing spread. For CAD, WTI is the number that moves the terms of trade; for JPY/EUR importers, Brent.
chapters.meaning: What changed: Saturday widened the maritime war. The IRGC navy claimed a supertanker struck naval mines while exiting Hormuz via an 'unauthorized' route — the first mine use of the campaign — but the vessel is unnamed and no independent source has confirmed the blast: a claim, not a fact. Separately verified: a Marshall Islands-flagged tanker was struck by projectile Saturday evening (UKMTO Warning 162-26) — the 18th confirmed Iranian hit since Sept 29 — and a US fighter jet disabled the Panama-flagged M/V Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman after it ignored blockade warnings (Reuters). CENTCOM says 4 vessels disabled, 135 turned around, and 10 IRGC-linked shadow tankers destroyed since July 14; strait transits sit at 2+ month lows. Thread: Brent settled Friday at $104.72 (+$0.44, +2.42% on the week); the ~$13 gap to WTI (~$91.8) is the geopolitical/shipping premium living in Brent while landlocked WTI barely feels it. ING's read from Friday stands: the market is 'reluctant to price out the geopolitical premium' above $100. What it means: the number that matters isn't either price, it's the spread — past $15 means Hormuz risk is back in force, toward $5 means the premium is truly unwinding. One physical counterweight: Hormuz flows ran 19.5–22.5M bpd Sep 27–29 (Kpler), above pre-war levels — the disruption so far is in the risk, not the barrels. The OFAC diesel license (General License 135, through Apr 7 2027) is now the paper behind the Trump–Putin diesel deal: a fuel-market sideshow for crude (~6M barrels ≈ 1.5 days of US demand). And Trump has now made the deal explicitly conditional on Kyiv restraining its refinery strikes — telling Zelenskyy it was 'time for Ukraine to get a new president' after blaming the strikes for the diesel surge.

chapters.fx: What to watch: a break back above $4,300 would signal the haven bid is broadening beyond dollar-weakness — historically a USD-negative, CHF/JPY-positive setup. Conversely, a hot CPI Wednesday that revives hike bets would likely knock gold back toward $4,000.
chapters.meaning: What changed: no price move (closed) — but the mine claim, tanker #18, and the Ocean Molica strike re-arm the war-hedge leg for the reopen. Thread: gold rose to ~$4,195 Friday on the full package — a softer dollar, easing yields, and the evening's escalation arriving together. It sits ~22% below January's $5,318 peak, after months bleeding lower as the Fed's hawkish hold kept real yields elevated and the dollar ripped to 18-month highs. What it means: Friday was the first day in a while gold worked as both trades at once — the anti-dollar and the war hedge. Saturday's news gives the haven leg fresh fuel into Sunday; CPI Wednesday decides the dollar leg.
